decisions.executionNote: Approach the left-side yellow nut with an elbow-up overhead arc; keep the right arm parked.
Finish downward alignment and descend over the yellow nut; leave jaws open for visual centering.
Correct the small wrist-view lateral error, close on the yellow nut, and lift to check retention.
The nut stayed on the table. Reopen, correct toward its center and grasp slightly lower, then make a short retention lift.
Lift the retained yellow nut clear and carry it to the central staging area without crossing the arms.
Set yellow down at the center, release and lift left away. Bring the right arm up in its own workspace for the handover.
Clear the left arm to its side while the right approaches the staged yellow nut from above. Stop above grasp height for visual correction.
Descend and close the right gripper on staged yellow, then lift a little to inspect retention. Move left above the blue nut with clearance.
Lift yellow clear and move it toward the right workspace to verify retention. Descend over the blue nut and close at its upper side faces.
Yellow was not retained. Recenter the open right gripper over its new table position at normal grasp height. Lift blue and keep it on the left while checking retention.
Blue is visibly retained. Refine right-hand yellow centering from the wrist image, close and lift while the left waits clear.
Carry retained yellow toward its matching right-side screw. Stage blue at the center for the next handover, keeping the arms separated.
Place and release blue at the center, then clear the left arm. Center yellow above its screw and lower cautiously to engagement height.
Make a small visual centering correction and start a slow clockwise tightening stroke with slight descent; park left clear of the center.
The yellow nut appears to have shifted in the jaws. Release and lift slightly to inspect its seating before another tightening stroke.
Yellow did not seat. Reset the wrist while approaching the fallen nut, then regrasp it for a more precise alignment.
Lift the regrasped yellow nut vertically and restore upright tool alignment; inspect retention and clearance from its screw before translating.
Yellow remains on the table. Reorient the open jaws away from the adjacent screw, center over the nut, and descend to grasp height.
Narrow the jaws to clear the nearby screw, make a small centering adjustment, grasp yellow, and lift vertically to test retention.
Recenter using the head and wrist views. Turn the jaw opening direction perpendicular to the adjacent screw, then descend and grasp yellow.
Lift yellow straight up with the gripper closed and inspect whether it is retained before moving over the screw.
Yellow is retained. Translate over the screw using the upright axis, then lower to just above the thread entry for a fresh alignment check.
Refine the lateral offset seen through the nut, lower a few millimeters, and attempt a short slow clockwise engagement stroke.
Continue the aligned clockwise stroke within wrist limits, then open and reset the wrist without translating, checking that yellow remains seated.
Yellow remains aligned after release. Regrasp at its settled height and make another slow clockwise tightening stroke.
Release the seated yellow nut, reset wrist yaw with open jaws, and regrasp for another clockwise stroke without moving its axis.
Turn yellow clockwise through another controlled stroke, following the thread downward by only two millimeters and keeping the axis fixed.
Reset the open wrist for another tightening stroke; yellow stays coaxial with its screw, but full fastening depth is not yet certain.
Apply another clockwise tightening stroke with minimal downward follow, then release yellow to inspect its final seating.
Lift clear of the released yellow assembly and reset yaw while moving above the staged blue nut; keep left parked.
Approach the centrally staged blue nut, descend vertically with open jaws, and close at grasp height. Yellow is left released on its matching screw.
Lift blue clear and carry it above its matching right-side screw while maintaining the grasp and upright axis.
Correct blue's lateral alignment and lower slowly toward the screw tip, pausing before rotation to inspect coaxial seating.
Center the blue screw tip within the nut and begin a slow clockwise engagement stroke with only a small downward follow.
Correct the blue tip's remaining wrist-view offset, make a short engagement turn, then release and reset yaw to inspect whether the nut stays seated.
The blue nut is tilted rather than seated. After the interrupted reset, use smaller yaw steps and regrasp without further tightening.
Blue fell beside its screw. Reopen and approach the nut's new position, rotating the jaw opening direction to avoid the adjacent screw.
Use the wrist-view offset to recenter on blue, close at nut height, and lift without turning to check the grasp.
Blue is visibly retained. Translate above its screw axis and lower slowly to inspect the tip through the nut before turning.
The blue tip is still outside the hole. Make a small two-axis wrist-view correction and pause without turning to verify alignment.
The blue tip now appears centered through the nut. Apply a slow clockwise stroke with a three-millimeter downward follow, holding the axis fixed.
Blue shifted off axis during turning. Lift slightly, correct the visible tip offset, and lower without rotation to re-establish alignment.
With the blue tip nearly centered, lower gently through entry while making a short clockwise stroke, keeping the lateral axis fixed.
Follow the blue nut down slowly with a short clockwise turn, then release to test whether it remains supported coaxially on the screw.
Blue remains near the screw but is tilted. Reset the open wrist with slight clearance and regrasp its side faces to restore a level grip before tightening.
Blue slipped off the screw. Open and withdraw above the table to obtain an unobstructed view before regrasping the loose nut.
Approach the loose blue nut at its observed new position, with jaws oriented away from the neighboring screw; pause open at grasp height.
Refine blue centering from the wrist view, close on its side faces, and lift vertically to confirm retention.
Bring the retained blue nut back above the screw using the visible tip location, then pause just above insertion height for precise alignment.
Lift free of side contact, correct the remaining wrist-view offset, and lower again without rotation so the blue screw enters the nut rather than its rim.
Make a final small centering correction, lower onto the blue screw, and attempt a short clockwise engagement stroke while monitoring alignment.
Adjust the small remaining blue tip offset, then continue clockwise with shallow downward follow while keeping the nut upright.
Blue has lost coaxial alignment. Lift slightly, shift toward the visible screw axis, and lower without rotation to inspect engagement.
Correct the remaining fore-aft wrist-view offset with a short clearance lift, then lower blue without turning to avoid pushing against the screw rim.
The last correction moved the screw farther from the opening. Lift fully clear, restore vertical tool alignment, reverse that offset toward the screw, and lower without turning.
Blue has slipped within the grip and remains offset. Move it to a clear right-side table area to set it down and establish a centered upright grasp.
Release blue in the clear staging area and lift away so it can settle upright; inspect its center before making a fresh grasp.
Recenter over the settled blue nut using the head view, descend vertically, and close for a fresh upright grasp away from the screw.
Blue is caught at the jaw edge rather than centered. Reopen with clearance, shift toward its wrist-view center, and regrasp without turning.
Lift blue without changing its orientation and carry it above the screw, checking the nut's position within the grip before lowering.
Compensate for the nut's small in-gripper offset and lower gradually over blue's screw, without rotating before seating is visible.
Lower blue gently without rotation so the visible tip can enter the opening, then release briefly to test seating before further tightening.
Blue now stays upright on the screw after release. Center the open jaws around its settled position, regrasp, and apply a short clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue tightening the now-supported blue nut, then release and reset yaw with open jaws while keeping its axis fixed.
Blue remains upright after release. Regrasp and apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke with minimal downward follow.
Release blue and reset the wrist for another tightening stroke, preserving the seated nut's position and elbow-up configuration.
Continue a controlled clockwise blue tightening stroke with the gripper closed and less than one millimeter of downward follow.
Reset the open wrist around the seated blue nut and regrasp for a final tightening stroke; avoid further vertical pressure.
Apply a final clockwise blue tightening stroke without downward motion, then release the nut to leave the assembly supported on the table.
Leave blue released, lift clear, and approach the remaining purple nut in the right workspace while resetting to a vertical grasp orientation.
After the continuity interruption, descend first to reduce reach, then use small increments to center the open right gripper over purple.
Use the wrist-view offset to center the purple nut between the jaws, close, and lift vertically to verify retention.
Purple is retained. Carry it to the central handover area and lower it onto the table, keeping the left arm clear.
Release purple at the center and clear the right arm upward and rightward. Bring the left arm toward the handover area only as space opens.
Center the open left gripper over staged purple and descend to grasp height. Move the right arm farther into its own workspace to leave clear handover space.
Make a small purple centering adjustment, close and lift to check retention. Return the empty right arm toward its origin while keeping the arms separated.
Carry the retained purple nut above its matching left-side screw with clearance. Settle the empty right arm at origin.
